{{nihongo|'''Housono Shrine'''|祝園神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamashiro Province]].

'''Housono Shrine''' (ほうそのじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Seika, Kyoto|ar|سيكا (كيوتو)|arz|سيكا, كيوتو|de|Seika (Kyōto)|es|Seika (Kioto)|fa|سیکا، کیوتو|fr|Seika (Kyoto)|id|Seika, Kyōto|it|Seika (Giappone)|ja|精華町|ko|세이카정|ms|Seika, Kyoto|my|ဆဲခမြို့၊ ကျိုတို|pl|Seika|ru|Сейка (посёлок)|sv|Seika|tl|Seika, Kyoto|tr|Seika|uk|Сейка (Кіото)|ur|سائیکا، کیوٹو|zh|精華町|zh_yue|精華町|qid=Q1203237}}, {{ill|Sōraku District, Kyoto|ar|منطقة سووراكو (كيوتو)|ceb|Sōraku-gun|es|Distrito de Sōraku|fr|District de Sōraku|id|Distrik Sōraku, Kyōto|it|Distretto di Sōraku|ja|相楽郡|ko|소라쿠군|lt|Soraku apskritis|my|ဆိုးရခုဒေသ၊ ကျိုတို|pl|Powiat Sōraku|ru|Сораку|uk|Повіт Сораку|zh|相樂郡|zh_yue|相樂郡|qid=Q1154661}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}. It is enshrined at the place where {{ill|Prince Takehaniyasuhiko|Q11545865|qid=Q11545865}}, said to have rebelled in the era of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, was reportedly defeated<ref>''National Shrine Directory Vol. 2'', National Shrine Directory Publication Society, {{ill|1977|Q2481|qid=Q2481}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 52), p.91</ref>.

Its shrine crest is “Sagari Fuji.”

=== Enshrined deities ===
It enshrines three deities: {{ill|Takemikazuchi|de|Takemikazuchi|eo|Takemikazuĉi|es|Takemikazuchi|fa|تاکه‌میکازوچی|fr|Takemikazuchi|id|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|pl|Takemikazuchi|pt|Takemikadzuchi|ru|Такэмикадзути|zh|建御雷|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|fr|Futsunushi|it|Futsunushi|ja|経津主神|mni|ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯨꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Futsunushi|ru|Фуцунуси|zh|經津主神|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}}.

=== History ===
The founding period is unknown, but the {{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|ja|新抄格勅符抄|qid=Q11502312}} (record of shrine households, decree of {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} 1 ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}})) includes “Housono deity, four households, {{ill|Yamashiro Province|cs|Provincie Jamaširo|de|Provinz Yamashiro|es|Provincia de Yamashiro|fa|ولایت یاماشیرو|fr|Province de Yamashiro|gl|Provincia de Yamashiro|hak|Yamashiro-koet|id|Provinsi Yamashiro|it|Yamashiro (provincia)|ja|山城国|ko|야마시로국|lt|Jamaširo žemė|ms|Yamashiro Province|nl|Yamashiro (provincie)|pt|Província de Yamashiro|ru|Ямасиро (провинция)|simple|Yamashiro Province|sk|Jamaširo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамаширо|tr|Yamashiro (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямашіро|wuu|山城国|zh|山城國|zh_min_nan|Yamasiro-kok|zh_yue|山城國|qid=Q749276}},” so it is presumed to have existed in the {{ill|Nara period|af|Nara-tydperk|ar|فترة نارا|bcl|Panahon nin Nara|bg|Нара (период)|bn|নারা যুগ|ca|Període Nara|ckb|سەردەمی نارا|cs|Období Nara|de|Nara-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Νάρα|eo|Epoko de Nara|es|Período Nara|eu|Nara aroa|fa|دوره نارا|fi|Nara-kausi|fr|Époque de Nara|gl|Período Nara|he|תקופת נארה|hr|Nara (razdoblje)|hu|Nara-kor|id|Zaman Nara|it|Periodo Nara|ja|奈良時代|jv|Periodhe Nara|ko|나라 시대|lt|Nara laikotarpis|ml|നാറ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Nara|nl|Naraperiode|nn|Naratida|no|Nara-perioden|oc|Periòde de Nara|pl|Nara (okres)|ps|نارا|pt|Período Nara|ro|Perioada Nara|ru|Период Нара|sh|Nara period|simple|Nara period|sk|Obdobie Nara|sl|Obdobje Nara|sr|Нара период|sv|Naraperioden|th|ยุคนาระ|tl|Panahong Nara|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Nala|tr|Nara Dönemi|uk|Період Нара|ur|نارا دور|vi|Thời kỳ Nara|war|Panahon Nara|wuu|奈良时代|zh|奈良時代|zh_min_nan|Nara sî-tāi|zh_yue|奈良時代|qid=Q189178}}. The {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} deity register records it as “Housono Shrine”<ref>Place Names of Kyoto Prefecture, p.107</ref>.

=== Rituals ===
Every year for three days from the {{ill|Yang Wood Monkey|af|Houtaap (astrologie)|cdo|Gák-sĭng|de|Holz-Affe|fr|Singe de bois|hak|Kap-sṳ̂n|ja|甲申|ko|갑신|nds|Holt-Aap|vi|Giáp Thân|za|Gyapsaen|zh|甲申|zh_min_nan|Kap-sin|zh_yue|甲申|qid=Q1062011}} day of {{ill|Japanese New Year|ar|رأس السنة اليابانية|az|Yaponiyada Yeni il|bcl|Bagong Taon kan Hapon|bg|Японска нова година|ca|Cap d'any japonès|da|Japansk nytår|de|Japanisches Neujahrsfest|es|Año Nuevo japonés|eu|Japoniar urteberri-egun|fa|سال نوی ژاپنی|fr|Nouvel An japonais|hu|Japán újév|hy|Ամանորը Ճապոնիայում|id|Tahun baru Jepang|it|Capodanno giapponese|ja|正月|ko|쇼가쓰|mn|Японы шинэ жил|ms|Tahun Baru Jepun|pl|Shōgatsu|pt|Ano-novo japonês|ro|Anul Nou Japonez|ru|Новый год в Японии|simple|Japanese New Year|sr|Нова година у Јапану|ta|சப்பானியப் புத்தாண்டு|th|ตรุษญี่ปุ่น|tr|Japon Yeni Yılı|uk|Новий рік у Японії|uz|Yaponiyada yangi yil|vi|Tết Nhật Bản|zh|日本新年|qid=Q701398}}, the {{ill|Igomori Festival|ja|いごもり祭|qid=Q22123234}} is held. بطولية|as|কিংবদন্তি|ast|Lleenda|ay|Jawari|az|Əfsanə|azb|افسانه|ba|Легенда|bat_smg|Legenda|be|Легенда|bg|Легенда|bn|কিংবদন্তি|br|Richenn|ca|Llegenda|ceb|Leyenda|ckb|ئەفسانە|cs|Pověst|cv|Легенда|da|Legende|de|Legende|dsb|Powěsć|el|Θρύλος|eo|Legendo|es|Leyenda|et|Legend|eu|Elezahar|fa|افسانه|fi|Legenda|fr|Légende|fy|Leginde|gd|Ùirsgeul|gl|Lenda|guw|Otàngblo|he|סיפור quỷ|war|Dimunyu|wuu|邪灵|xmf|დემონი|zh|邪靈|zh_yue|邪靈|qid=Q177413}} and remained in this area ruining fields, so the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=villagers}} secluded themselves in ritual abstinence to pacify the spirit<ref name=tamino>{{Cite journal |和書|author=Kentarō Tamino |title=Structure and Change of Tug-of-War Rituals: A Case of Seika, Sōraku District, Kyoto |journal=Japan Society of Physical Education Conference Proceedings |publisher=Japan Society of Physical Education |year=1997 |volume=48 |issue=48th Conference (1997) |pages=639 |naid=110001903306 |doi=10.20693/jspeconf.48.0_639 |url=https://doi.org/10.20693/jspeconf.48.0_639}} {{ja icon}}</ref>. In old times, during the festival, {{ill|Cattle|Q830|qid=Q830}} and {{ill|Horse|Q726|qid=Q726}} were entrusted to neighboring villages, all {{ill|Sound|Q11461|qid=Q11461}} was forbidden, and people stayed in seclusion eating only {{ill|Buddhist cuisine|Q1326339|qid=Q1326339}}<ref name=tamino/>. On day 1, priests perform the “Furoi rite” in darkness; on day 2, the “Mita rite” with torches; and on day 3, the “tug-of-war rite”<ref name=tamino/>. The rope is a huge ring about 1 meter in diameter made by wrapping split bamboo with straw and attaching six bamboo poles; {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655|lt=parishioners}} divide into north and south sides and hold three tug-of-war rounds. After the winner is decided, the rope is carried to {{ill|Izumori|Q20043114|qid=Q20043114}}, said to be the execution site of Takehaniyasuhiko, and burned.

* {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|Q502125|qid=Q502125}}{{ill|Katamachi Line|Q1073379|qid=Q1073379}}, get off at {{ill|Hōsono Station|Q855574|qid=Q855574}}, 20 minutes on foot.
